papers.title: Noise-Induced Restoration of Entropy Concavity Near Gaussian Equilibrium
papers.abstract: We study a quantitative form of noise-induced restoration of entropy concavity for one-dimensional nonequilibrium states relaxing toward a Gaussian thermal equilibrium. A partially thermalized state is modeled by $X_q=\sqrt q\,X+\sqrt{1-q}\,G$, where $G$ is Gaussian equilibrium noise and $q$ is the retained signal fraction. For two independently prepared copies we ask when the entropy of the mixed state $h(\sqrt{1-t}\,X_q+\sqrt t\,Y_q)$ is concave in the mixing parameter. The problem is motivated by entropy geometry along Ornstein--Uhlenbeck/Fokker--Planck relaxation, where the relative score is the nonequilibrium thermodynamic force and relative Fisher information is entropy-production rate. We derive an exact symmetric endpoint-curvature formula, separating a nonnegative Ornstein--Uhlenbeck restoring term from a fourth-cumulant correction, and extend it to nonsmooth generalized-Gaussian states $e^{-a|x|^p}$ for $p>3/2$. For half thermalization of a symmetric log-concave input, posterior-variance identities give a quantitative outer-region theorem confining any endpoint obstruction to two explicitly bounded near-equilibrium sectors. We also give spectral and MMSE reformulations of the auxiliary inequality $A\ge2\delta$, prove it in an explicit nonlinear neighborhood of Gaussian equilibrium, and show how it sharpens the endpoint bounds. The main all-mixing result concerns the leading symmetric non-Gaussian Hermite mode: for $p_a=\phiG(1+a\He_4)$, $0<a\le10^{-2}$, we prove strict entropy concavity for every $0<t<1$ and every $0<q\le5/8$, hence throughout the currently unresolved symmetric range $0<q\le4/7$ for this explicit nonequilibrium family. Numerical searches over broader log-concave families are reported only as supporting evidence.
authors: Fayez Abu-Ajamieh

papers.title: QMBL: the Quantum Many-Body Leaderboard. A live record of published ground-state energies for lattice Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: In condensed matter physics, scientists explore phase diagrams of matter through various methods (analysis, numerics, experiment) and achieve consensus when enough methods agree. The quality of variational results for quantum many-body ground states is mainly judged by energy values and respective errors. Here, we present QMBL, the Quantum Many-Body Leaderboard (https://www.qmbl.org), serving as the energy layer of the scientific consensus. It is a maintained, interactive record of published ground-state energies for lattice Hamiltonians. The latest release v0.4.0 holds 1434 energies on 395 instances of six model families and collects all of the community's efforts into one view. Of those instances 153 have no exact solution and any new record serves as a direct improvement to an open science problem. They are the targets of a companion benchmark, QMBL: Open Problems.
authors: Tristan Zerweck, Juan Carrasquilla

papers.title: Thermodynamics of coupled electromagnetic and mass fields
papers.abstract: We formulate a unified thermodynamic framework for chemical, mechanical, and electromagnetic transport by extending the Gibbs--Duhem relation to include kinetic free-energy contributions associated with material and field motion. The resulting kinetic Gibbs--Duhem relation establishes a thermodynamic connection between free-energy variations, generalized chemical potentials, pressure, and transport momentum, while preserving the invariance of the system free energy under changes of reference frame. Within a Lagrangian formulation of free-energy evolution, the relation provides a common structure for diffusion, momentum transport, and electromagnetic dynamics. For nonuniform chemical systems, the framework recovers the coupling between Cahn--Hilliard dynamics and the Korteweg stress arising from composition gradients. Its extension to electromagnetic systems incorporates electric, magnetic, charge, and mechanical contributions into the same thermodynamic formulation, yielding a unified description of electromagnetic and momentum evolution. The framework further separates dissipative from nondissipative transport and establishes a common thermodynamic form for mechanical and electromagnetic propagation. In the isentropic limit, the characteristic propagation velocity is determined by the derivative of the thermodynamic pressure with respect to density, yielding the speed of sound for mechanical systems and the speed of light for electromagnetic systems. These results show that kinetic contributions can be incorporated consistently into the Gibbs--Duhem framework, providing a common thermodynamic basis for coupled chemical, mechanical, and electromagnetic transport without introducing separate thermodynamic principles for each mechanism.
authors: Fei Wang

papers.title: General Relativity in Three Lines
papers.abstract: We show that complex general relativity can be formulated directly in terms of three affine lines assigned to each spacetime point. The lines are represented by Pl\"ucker bivectors, and Urbantke's construction applied to the associated two-forms reconstructs the conformal spacetime metric. Starting from the chiral Pleba\'nski action, the simplicity constraints turn the three two-forms into a null internal basis of simple bivectors and thereby into three projective lines. A $3+1$ decomposition then yields a first-order canonical theory whose configuration variable is the weighted triple of lines and whose conjugate variable is a line momentum. The resulting constraint system consists of three internal Gauss constraints, three vector constraints, and one Hamiltonian constraint. A notable feature of the line formulation is that the equation obtained by varying the line momentum is pointwise algebraic after the spatial integrations by parts. Consequently the momentum can be eliminated explicitly wherever the corresponding Legendre map is invertible, giving a second-order action whose only dynamical configuration variable is the weighted triple of lines. The line curvature separates naturally into a cosmological trace and the Weyl matrix of the selected chiral sector. The Legendre map becomes singular on a distinguished null-evolution locus where the spacetime metric remains nondegenerate. There its rank drops from nine to six, giving three algebraic compatibility conditions. We construct a finite invariant partial Legendre transform and a smooth constrained second-order continuation through this locus. This analysis provides a regular framework for regimes in which the evolution direction becomes null and may be useful in the study of near-horizon geometries and related gravitational phenomena.
authors: Pawel Nurowski

papers.title: Dynamical entropy and thermodynamics of causal diamonds
papers.abstract: We study the dynamical entropy of causal diamonds using Wald-Zoupas charges and fluxes on their null boundaries. For a chosen boundary symplectic potential, the boost charge defines an entropy made of an area term plus an expansion correction, which reduces to one quarter of the area at the edge on the diamond. In Einstein gravity, we find an exact balance law relating the entropy on any two cuts of the null boundary to a signed flux, so the entropy decreases only when this flux is non-negative. We obtain a linearised physical process first law without assuming a background Killing symmetry, both in the presence and absence of external matter; and extend it for semiclassical gravity based on the improved quantum null energy condition. We also examine causal diamonds in maximally symmetric spacetimes and in Einstein-scalar gravity.
authors: Avik Chakraborty, Pratik K. Das, Manavendra Mahato

papers.title: Geodesics in Black-Hole Spacetimes: A Qualitative Classification Using Vieta's Formulae
papers.abstract: This monograph classifies the geodesics of the Schwarzschild, Kerr and Schwarzschild-de Sitter black holes without solving for their turning points. In all three spacetimes, the radial and polar motions are governed by polynomials whose coefficients depend only on the constants of motion, and the qualitative behavior of a geodesic is fixed by the pattern of their roots. We read this pattern directly off the coefficients, using Vieta's formulae together with the discriminant, Descartes' rule of signs, and the values of the polynomials at the horizons and at infinity. In Schwarzschild spacetime, the reciprocals of the radial roots of every non-radial geodesic add up to $1/(2M)$, which gives the third root of a bound orbit in closed form and the separatrix $p=6+2e$. In Kerr spacetime, the signs of the coefficients show that no radially bound orbit has $\varepsilon^2\geq1$ and that vortical geodesics, timelike or null, have no radial turning point; a positive discriminant is necessary but not sufficient for bound motion, and Descartes' rule applied at the event horizon gives the exact criterion. Spherical orbits and their stability, the equatorial ISCO and light rings, and the photon shell follow from the same relations. In Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime, the timelike radial polynomial is a quintic with exactly one negative root, a bound branch requires $\varepsilon^2+\Lambda L^2/3<1$, and both marginally stable circular orbits lie beyond $6M$. Most of these results are known; the aim is to show that a single, elementary algebraic route leads to all of them. The text is meant for graduate students who have taken a first course in general relativity, and each chapter ends with worked examples.
authors: Oliver F. Piattella

papers.title: Semiclassical Analysis of Wave Dynamics via Wigner Transforms: Applications to the Quantum Harmonic, Anharmonic, and Dirac Oscillator
papers.abstract: In this Master's thesis, we give a pedagogical introduction to the semiclassical analysis of wave dynamics in single-band and multi-band systems. We show how the semiclassical evolutions of Wigner functions can approximate the dynamics of wave packet centers and wave packet deformations. Three systems of increasing complexity are considered: the quantum harmonic oscillator and the quantum anharmonic oscillator as single-band systems, and the Dirac oscillator as a two-band system. We explain the origins of the first-order semiclassical corrections (Moyal, Littlejohn-Flynn, and Berry) in the equations of motion and examine their effects on predictive accuracy. Another focus is set on the conditions for validity of the semiclassical analysis. For both the quantum anharmonic and the Dirac oscillators, a dimensionless parameter controlling the accuracy of the approximation is identified. In multi-band systems, the formalism applies only to states within a single adiabatic subspace, which, for the Dirac oscillator, corresponds to an energy branch. This motivates the construction of single-branch almost coherent states: approximately Gaussian wave packets formed by superpositions of states from a single energy branch. Their centers undergo oscillations with an aperiodic envelope. These states enable comparison between semiclassical Wigner function evolution and the commonly used Sundaram-Niu formalism. We show that semiclassical Wigner function evolution captures deformation-related dynamics, including the initial decay of oscillations, which the Sundaram-Niu formalism cannot describe by construction. Additionally, exact quantum evolution reveals partial relocalization of these single-branch almost coherent states, a phenomenon that cannot be captured by the semiclassical evolution.
authors: August Burg

papers.title: Dilaton-Axion Wormhole Partition Function Away from the BPS Endpoint
papers.abstract: I determine the leading finite-radius correction to the two-boundary response of a charged axion wormhole near its BPS endpoint. With $\delta=a_*^2$, exact radial matching in a product axion--dilaton/saxion system gives a boundary eigenvalue that vanishes as $O(\delta)$ and an off-diagonal Hessian entry of order $O(\delta^2)$. Their combination produces a cross-boundary covariance linear in $\delta$, with a negative first sub-leading correction on the branch studied here. I determine the semiclassical range in which the quadratic approximation remains controlled and identify the first finite-radius angular resonance, $\delta^2\log(\delta/\delta_0)$. Under a uniform rescaling of all active charges, the coefficient of the linear cross-boundary response scales as the inverse square of the charge scale. I then average the inverse response over the chiral Gaussian ensemble describing the BPS endpoint. Boundary reduction preserves the hard-edge index. Multiplication by the matched BPS sector weight converts the normalized response into the leading finite-radius two-source coefficient.
authors: Soo-Jong Rey

papers.title: Angular Momenta in $4+1$ Vacuum Critical Collapse
papers.abstract: We investigate the critical collapse of gravitational waves that carry angular momenta. Working in five-dimensional vacuum Einstein gravity under an SU$(2)\times\mathbb Z_4$ symmetry ansatz, we numerically evolve several families of initial data near the threshold of black-hole formation. Near-critical data approaches the discretely self-similar Bizo\'n-Chmaj-Schmidt solution, which is irrotational. We find that the near-threshold mass scaling has a universal critical exponent, but the angular-momentum scaling has one of two critical exponents, depending on the family of initial data. The angular-momentum critical exponents are therefore not universal under this symmetry ansatz. Our results agree with predictions from perturbation theory about the critical solution.
authors: Oscar J. C. Dias, Carsten Gundlach, Jorge E. Santos, Benson Way

papers.title: Typical Superpositions are Magical
papers.abstract: The non-stabilizerness, or "magic", of a quantum state is a common metric for the hardness of simulation on a classical computer, and is often quantified by the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy (SRE). We show how random superpositions of classically simulable states saturate the SRE to the symmetry-restricted Haar-random maximum. For any large-$N$ random pure-state ensemble satisfying the conditions of Schur's lemma, the average SRE of the $m$-component superposition $\langle M_2(m)\rangle=N-\log_2[\langle W(m)\rangle]$ is governed by an average witness $\langle W(m)\rangle$ that universally decomposes into a Haar floor and an ensemble-specific excess. As the number of components $m$ increases, the excess is suppressed, resulting in a logarithmic scaling of the SRE before plateauing at the Haar-valued maximum. We derive a general closed form for $\langle W(m)\rangle$ in the thermodynamic limit, and numerically verify our result for random stabilizer states and random Gaussian states.
authors: Joshuah T. Heath, Andrew Urilyon, Damien Quinn, Graham Kells

papers.title: A non-prompt null ray cures its own singularity
papers.abstract: In AdS/CFT correlators, bulk cone singularities arise when two points that are timelike separated on the AdS boundary may be connected by a null geodesic through the bulk. We consider corrections to these correlators away from the $G_N\to 0$ limit arising from the backreaction of this null geodesic. A peculiar property of this geodesic is that it is not prompt, meaning that there exist points on it that are timelike separated. This implies that it may gravitationally affect itself. We show that this leads to an energy-dependent delay in the time elapsed along this geodesic. This coupled with possible inelastic effects due to gravitational radiation are the leading mechanisms that resolve the singularity. The resolved singularity is accompanied by oscillations and hence zeroes in the real and imaginary parts of the correlator. We comment on the role that additional inelastic effects play in damping these oscillations. Finally, we provide a concrete example in $2+1$D where we can compute the energy-dependent time delay effect explicitly by studying the boundary graviton mode.
authors: Gauri Batra

papers.title: Exploring Quantum Phase Transitions Beyond Landau Theory on a Quantum Processor
papers.abstract: Direct continuous quantum phase transitions between phases that break distinct symmetries challenge the conventional Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm and provide a framework for deconfined quantum criticality. Here, we investigate a Landau-forbidden ferromagnetic-to-valence-bond-solid (FM-VBS) transition in a frustrated one-dimensional spin chain using superconducting quantum processors. Combining matrix-product-state-assisted circuit preparation with quantum-hardware measurements, we resolve the suppression of long-range ferromagnetic correlations and the redistribution of competing-order fluctuations across the transition. Distance-resolved correlations and finite-size analyses reveal signatures consistent with critical behavior. We further extend our investigation to nonequilibrium dynamics, directly preparing dimerized states and tracking the evolution of VBS order and joint FM-VBS fluctuations under local unitary interactions. Our results establish a versatile quantum-hardware framework for probing competing orders, critical correlations, and many-body dynamics beyond conventional Landau theory.
authors: Ruizhe Shen, Yin Zhong, Ching Hua Lee

papers.title: Topological Aspects of the $c=2$ Model in the Continuum and on the Lattice
papers.abstract: We discuss the continuum two-dimensional conformal field theory, whose target space is a two-torus. In addition to its standard zero-form internal symmetries, the model also has a $-1$-form symmetry associated with its $\theta$-parameter, which is also known as a background $B$-field. These symmetries combine into a higher group with anomalies. A spatially winding $B$-field generically breaks the spatial translation symmetry completely, and reduces the continuous target-space (internal) momentum symmetry to a (projectively realized) discrete subgroup. When $B$ varies linearly, a discrete translation subgroup survives, and it combines with the internal symmetry into a non-Abelian group, while the other translations survive as non-invertible symmetries. Even though the model lacks the standard spatial translation symmetry, the non-invertible translation symmetry explains why it is solvable via a Fourier decomposition. We then consider a lattice version of this system, using its modified Villain formulation. Surprisingly, all these subtleties in the symmetries of the continuum model exist on a finite lattice. Finally, we discuss various generalizations of this model, demonstrating that the phenomena we uncovered are more broadly valid.
authors: Yichul Choi, Nathan Seiberg, Sahand Seifnashri, Wucheng Zhang

papers.title: Multi-Time States in Quantum and Operational Probabilistic Theories: An Axiomatic Framework
papers.abstract: Quantum states over time were introduced, in part, to extend Bayesian probability to quantum theory and have since found applications across diverse areas, ranging from quantum causality and open-system dynamics to tests of macroscopic realism. While axiomatic characterizations of these states exist for Markovian dynamics, a general framework accommodating non-Markovian dynamics is still lacking. Moreover, extending this framework beyond quantum mechanics to general physical theories also remains elusive. In this work, we develop an axiomatic framework for multi-time states within a class of operational probabilistic theories (OPTs) that includes quantum mechanics as a special case. Based on three assumptions---compositionality, reconstructibility, and spatio-temporal marginal consistency---the framework accommodates both Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics, and provides sufficient conditions to certify signaling and temporal memory within OPT. As a concrete application of our OPT framework, we fully characterize the unique multi-time state in boxworld and develop a method for Bayesian retrodiction of physical transformations there. Our general framework is consistent with quantum theory, reproducing several existing results. In the non-Markovian quantum dynamics, we establish a correspondence between multi-time states and the process-matrix framework, and fully characterize the multi-time states compatible with general dynamics. This correspondence also lets us infer quantum causal models from multi-time states, and as a proof of principle, we propose a semidefinite program to infer causal order from quantum multi-time states. These results provide a unified framework for studying spatio-temporal states, causal relations, and Bayesian reasoning within OPTs, with implications for both fundamental and applied research.
authors: Kaumudibikash Goswami, Archana Barvar, Manabendra Nath Bera

papers.title: Entropy Production and Thermalization in Heavy-Quark Langevin Dynamics
papers.abstract: Heavy quarks are often treated as Brownian probes of the quark-gluon plasma. We formulate the irreversible entropy balance of their momentum distribution and separate the production generated by collisions from the driving caused by an evolving medium. For linear dynamics the production splits into two positive contributions, from directed momentum and from the momentum width. A static bath obeys an exact H-theorem. A cooling bath adds an explicit driving term, and longitudinal Bjorken expansion enters as a separate kinematic drive rather than as collisional production. For a Bjorken temperature protocol we derive closed-form strong- and weak-coupling limits of the total production. At strong coupling it exceeds the initial relative entropy by a term linear in the relaxation time, whose quasistatic part has the thermodynamic-length form. At weak coupling it vanishes inversely with the relaxation time. A positive strong-coupling slope therefore guarantees maximal dissipation at intermediate coupling. The same structure holds for a relativistic Fokker-Planck equation with a J\"uttner stationary state, solved numerically for charm and bottom quarks under the temperature protocol. Linear-response coefficients computed from the static generator reproduce both limits, and the numerical entropy balance is satisfied to high accuracy.
authors: A. M. Silva

papers.title: Superstring theory in $AdS_5\times S^5$ background: half-BPS vertex operators
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct all vertex operators associated with the gravity supermultiplet in the $AdS_5 \times S^5$ background, relevant for worldsheet scattering amplitude computations, via global $PSU(2,2|4)$ transformations. Although one such operator was previously constructed in the pure spinor formalism using a special superspace parametrization, implementing the full global symmetries proved challenging due to the mixing of bosonic and fermionic coordinates. We resolve this issue by introducing a judicious sequence of reparametrizations that disentangle these coordinates. We then advance the formulation of superstring theory in this background by constructing the corresponding integrated vertex operators in both the pure spinor and the B-RNS-GSS formalisms.
authors: Thiago Fleury, Lucas N. S. Martins, Dennis Zavaleta

papers.title: No cosmic horizons from a strengthened higher-dimensional strong energy condition
papers.abstract: Time-dependent supergravity compactifications lie beyond the setting of the Gibbons/Maldacena-Nu\~nez no-de Sitter theorem and can even support eternal cosmic acceleration, raising the question of whether they can also produce future cosmic horizons. For general higher-dimensional matter, the strong energy condition alone does not exclude such horizons. Here, we demonstrate that a theory fulfilling a strengthened version of the strong energy condition cannot be compactified down to a lower-dimensional theory able to support a future cosmic horizon. For 10d and 11d supergravities reduced to at least four large spacetime dimensions, this energy condition is fulfilled by the sources that already fulfill the strong energy condition in the higher-dimensional theory. Our assumption on the dimensional reduction is that it is performed on a smooth compact and boundaryless space.
authors: Flavio Tonioni

papers.title: Resonant pair production and flat band melting in a driven Rydberg chain
papers.abstract: We study a Rydberg chain subjected to a two-tone periodic drive of the detuning $\Delta(t)$ and Rabi frequency $\Omega(t)$ at frequencies $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2=\nu \omega_1$ respectively with $\nu \in \mathbf{Z}$. In the strong Rydberg blockade limit, such a system reduces to the PXP model and exhibits exact Floquet flat band. Here we determine, using a time-dependent Schrieffer-Wolff transformation, the domain of validity of such PXP dynamics once the blockade-violating processes are taken into account. We study the melting of such flat bands in the presence of strong, but finite, blockade strength. Using Floquet perturbation theory (FPT), we identify two mechanisms for such melting; the first occurs due to the presence of many-body resonances involving resonant production of nearest-neighbor Rydberg excitation pairs while the second involves virtual processes that access intermediate states with such pairs. Our analytical FPT results match with those obtained using exact diagonalization on a finite chain. We study the dynamics for $|{\rm vac}\rangle$ (Fock state with no Rydberg excitation), $|{\mathbb {Z}}_2\rangle$, and $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ (Fock states with Rydberg excitations on alternate and every third site respectively) initial states. We find that $|{\rm vac}\rangle$ shows exceptional stability against resonant pair formation while $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ exhibits flat band melting via virtual processes away from the direct resonances. We find oscillatory dynamics with large time period for the $|{\mathbb {Z}}_2\rangle$ initial state and the presence of Floquet scars that have large overlap with $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ state; these phenomena occur due to processes that are absent in the PXP limit. We propose measurement of nearest neighbor pair correlation functions using Rydberg atom quantum simulator platforms as an accessible experimental probe for these effects.
authors: Tista Banerjee, K. Sengupta

papers.title: The Singular Structure of Rapidity Distributions for Color-Singlet Production at N3LO
papers.abstract: We determine the universal singular structure of rapidity distributions for color-singlet production in hadron collisions through next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N3LO) in QCD. Our result captures the full singular contributions as either partonic momentum fraction approaches one, including the delta-function terms, while retaining the exact dependence on the other. The essential new ingredient is the complete calculation of the three-loop quark and gluon rapidity beam-function matching kernels. Our calculation is based on the strict collinear expansion of the partonic cross sections for Higgs boson and Drell-Yan production. We represent our results in terms of generalized polylogarithms as well as numerical series expansions. The resulting N3LO partonic coefficient functions apply to arbitrary color-singlet production processes with the process dependence entering through the hard function, which encodes the virtual corrections to the Born process.
authors: Federica Devoto, Bernhard Mistlberger, Gherardo Vita

papers.title: A thermally and perturbatively stable classical spin model in two dimensions
papers.abstract: We show that the 2D classical spin model constructed in arXiv:2605.10943 hosts many metastable states at non-zero temperature which are stable to arbitrary Hamiltonian perturbations, providing the first such example. Our proof relies on a recursive application of the cluster expansion.
authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, Ting-Chun Lin, Ryan Thorngren

papers.title: Quantum Periods from TBA and Continued Fractions
papers.abstract: We consider quantum A-periods of local ${\mathbb P}^1 \times {\mathbb P}^1$, or equivalently the generating function of constant terms for powers of the Laurent polynomial $x + x^{-1} + y + y^{-1}$ where $x$ and $y$ are $q$-commuting variables. We derive a number of new representations for these rich combinatorial and algebraic objects. First, we find that the well-known TBA equation encodes not only the A-period itself but also higher diagonal modes of the corresponding noncommutative Laurent polynomials. Second, we obtain new formulas for the period in terms of continued fractions and related orthogonal polynomials, as well as a nontrivial explicit recursion allowing its efficient computation. Finally, we compute quantum corrections to the classical Picard-Fuchs equation, and observe that holonomicity of the classical period does not generalise to $q$-holonomicity of its quantum counterpart. Applications to random walks on the Cayley graph of the Heisenberg group, and related new approaches to more efficient generative AI systems, are outlined.
authors: Alexander Chervov, Ilia Gaiur, Sergey Galkin, Fedor Levkovich-Maslyuk, Volodya Rubtsov, Shamil Shakirov

papers.title: Bulk-Defect Correspondence in Algebraic Classical Spin Liquids
papers.abstract: Local constraints in algebraic classical spin liquids give rise to singular momentum-space correlations. This so called pinch-point singularity carries a momentum-space winding number that determines the low-energy structure of the algebraic spin liquid. We show that nonmagnetic vacancies in two dimensions reveal this topological invariant in the real-space winding of the surrounding spin textures. Under explicit conditions, we prove this bulk-defect correspondence for rank-$n$ $\mathrm{U}(1)$ spin liquids and verify it numerically for the Coulomb spin liquids of the kagome and checkerboard lattices and the rank-2 $\mathrm{U}(1)$ spin liquid of the honeycomb-snowflake model. In this way we show that vacancies can be used as general probes for distinguishing the emergent gauge theories of strongly correlated classical disordered magnets.
authors: Rafael Flores-Calder\'on

papers.title: Perturbative Defect CFT Data in Scalar Models and Consistency Conditions
papers.abstract: We compute defect CFT data through $O(\epsilon)$ for scalar line defects in the $O(N)$, hypercubic, hypertetrahedral, $O(m)\times O(n)$ biconical, and $MN$ models in $d=4-\epsilon$. The $O(N)$ theory provides a benchmark; the datasets for the other four models are new. For the branches considered, we determine spectra, operator mixing, two- and three-point coefficients in a specified perturbative basis, and four-point functions with identical or paired external operators of integer dimension $n\leq2$ at $\epsilon=0$. We propose a framework for verifying perturbative defect CFT data by combining crossing symmetry, OPE reconstruction, and the applicable broken-symmetry integral identities. We also identify a new universal defect-direction sector whose one-loop data follow from the defect fixed-point equation. All applicable conditions are satisfied at the perturbative orders considered. The model data are collected in the supplemental notebook, defect_cft_data.nb.
authors: Ziwen Kong

papers.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
papers.abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $\mu$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.
authors: Shelby Klomp, Shafaq Gulzar Elahi, Scott Grudichak, Chethn Galla, Zhiyuan Wang, Mark Nguyen, George Winstone, Katarina Boskovic Guy, Emma Derrick, Maddox Wroblewski, Jacob Sprague, Andrew Laeuger, Jackson Larsen, Nancy Aggarwal, Shane L. Larson, Andrew A. Geraci

papers.title: Maximizing the spectral gap for free bosonic CFTs
papers.abstract: We study the spectral gap $\Delta_1$ of Narain CFTs, the smallest scaling dimension of a nonvacuum $U(1)^c_L\times U(1)^c_R$ primary, as a function on the Narain moduli space. Using the exceptional isomorphisms for $SO^+(2,2)$ and $SO^+(3,3)$, we prove the sharp bounds $\Delta_1\le 2/3$ at $c=2$ and $\Delta_1\le 3/4$ at $c=3$, with equality exactly at the $SU(3)_1$ and $SU(4)_1$ WZW models up to $O(c)\times O(c)$, and we describe local maxima of $\Delta_1$. For $4\le c\le 12$, we compare the Narain moduli space with the densest known Euclidean lattices: an arithmetic obstruction excludes five candidates, a computer-assisted classification shows that $E_8$, $K_{12}$, and $BW_{16}$ each admit a unique Narain structure up to lattice automorphisms, and a conceptual argument excludes the Leech lattice.
authors: Hyeongjoe Chu, Yuchan Jung

papers.title: Universal Threshold Laws for Dipolar Evaporation of Molecular Fermi Gases
papers.abstract: Fermi statistics suppress the elastic collisions that rethermalize a Fermi gas during evaporative cooling, creating a fundamental low-temperature bottleneck for producing quantum degenerate gases. We show that, for shielded single-component ultracold dipolar molecular Fermi gases in the Wigner threshold regime, this bottleneck is governed by universal threshold laws fixed by the effective dimensionality of the gas. In this regime, Fermi suppression of rethermalization scales quadratically with temperature in 3D but only linearly in 2D. Consequently, the thermalization-to-loss ratio is more favorable in 2D than in 3D, and these results suggest that 2D geometries are better suited for reaching deep degeneracy. We also present ab initio close-coupling calculations that agree well with experimental measurements on Fermi degenerate gases of KRb molecules, supporting our conclusions.
authors: Kevin B. Xu, John L. Bohn, Reuben R. W. Wang

papers.title: Circuit Synthesis for Variational Quantum Algorithms: The Depth of Algebra and Geometry
papers.abstract: The analysis of Hamiltonian Variational Ans\"atze centers on three fundamental questions: which states are exactly reachable from a given initial state, what native control depth suffices for local and global synthesis, and whether a bounded circuit extension can expose a direction of decreasing cost at a suboptimal output. We address these challenges by leveraging the dynamical Lie algebras (DLAs) associated with the circuits and the geometry of the initial state's orbit under the action of the corresponding dynamical Lie group $G$. We show that an initial state has a closed projective orbit whenever it is a nondegenerate eigenstate of a control Hamiltonian. Combined with asymptotic QAOA convergence, this guarantees exact, finite depth ground state preparation for architectures employing diagonal problem Hamiltonians and irreducible stoquastic mixers. We bound the number of native control exponentials required for local unitary synthesis and state preparation using DLA commutator filtration growth alongside reachable orbit dimensions. Complementing these local results, we construct global frameworks on invariant sectors equipped with full unitary or special unitary dynamical Lie algebras. These constructions yield explicit applications to Pauli-generated systems and constrained maximum independent set multi-angle QAOA circuits; specifically, we show that their native control costs are directly determined by commutator filtration depth and independent-set toggle-group geometry, respectively. Finally, if the dynamical Lie group is compact, the observable $H_P$ generates an admissible evolution ($iH_P \in \mathfrak{g}$, where $\mathfrak{g}$ is the DLA), and the projective orbit of the initial state contains a ground state ray of $H_P$, then a bounded depth, identity-initialized circuit extension exhibits either first-order descent or negative curvature at every suboptimal circuit output.
authors: Boris Tsvelikhovskiy

papers.title: Quantum-Classical Neural Networks for Solving Lindblad Master Equations
papers.abstract: Variational quantum algorithms have emerged as a promising approach for simulating open quantum systems, yet their expressive power and trainability remain poorly understood. We propose a variational framework for solving Lindblad master equations by minimizing a residual cost function using a compositional ansatz obtained by combining a classical neural network with a parameterized quantum circuit. The density matrix is represented through a purification on an enlarged Hilbert space, ensuring positivity, Hermiticity, and unit trace by construction, while all gradients are evaluated exactly via the parameter-shift rule. Beyond the algorithmic formulation, we derive an upper bound for the covering number of the proposed compositional model and compare it with that of purely quantum neural networks. Our analysis shows that the classical parametrization enlarges the effective hypothesis class while providing finer control over its complexity, thereby establishing a theoretical connection between expressivity, covering numbers, effective dimension, and the barren plateau phenomenon. Numerical experiments validate both the accuracy of the proposed method for representative Lindblad master equations and the theoretical predictions regarding gradient concentration. These results provide a unified variational and theoretical framework for the simulation of dissipative quantum dynamics using compositional quantum machine learning models.
authors: Rafael Florencio D\'iaz, Julio Guerrero Garc\'ia, Elvira Romera Guti\'errez

papers.title: Area Theorems for Quantum Error Correction
papers.abstract: The extrinsic information transfer (EXIT) and generalized EXIT (GEXIT) area theorems provide fundamental conservation laws that connect the rate of classical codes to the performance of maximum-a-posteriori decoding on binary memoryless channels. In this work, we generalize these area theorems to quantum error correction. We first develop a coset-entropy formalism for nested linear codes, where the message specifies a coset and encoder randomization selects a codeword within that coset. The area under the resulting coset (G)EXIT function equals the normalized dimension of the quotient. For stabilizer codes, the measured syndrome restricts the Pauli error but does not always determine its logical effect, and the remaining uncertainty is an entropy over logical correction classes. We show that this entropy equals a classical coset entropy associated with the stabilizer group and the Pauli operators that commute with it. The resulting quantum GEXIT function has area equal to the number of encoded qubits per channel use for any stabilizer code, and this applies to the depolarizing channel through its joint four-valued Pauli-error distribution. For CSS codes on the quantum erasure channel and under independent bit- and phase-flip noise, the logical correction problem separates into two binary coset-decoding problems. On the quantum erasure channel, the duality between the stabilizer group and the Pauli operators that commute with it gives a folding identity at complementary erasure probabilities. Using this and the area theorem, we derive an upper bound on the rate of code families with vanishing logical error probability that matches the capacity of the quantum erasure channel. For the depolarizing channel, we also derive a rate-dependent converse, using a connection between correction-class entropy and coherent information to establish an inequality involving the complementary channel.
authors: Avijit Mandal, Mert G\"{o}kduman, Henry D. Pfister

papers.title: Metric and Dispersive Dynamics of Phase Perturbations in Bohmian Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract: By linearizing the hydrodynamic equations associated with the Madelung transformation in the context of Bohmian dynamics, we derive an effective metric for the phase perturbation around a background state. We show that the metric previously obtained previously by the same authors arises naturally as a particular case of a more general structure, in which the complete functional variation of the quantum potential is retained and external classical potentials can be incorporated. This generalization preserves the dependence of the quantum potential on the density and its spatial derivatives, generating additional terms that introduce dispersive corrections and act as sources in the effective Klein-Gordon equation. To organize these contributions, we introduce differential operators that separate the local sector responsible for the effective geometry from the corrections associated with the complete functional structure of the quantum potential. We identify the conditions under which these additional terms become negligible, recovering homogeneous propagation and the effective geometry for the Gaussian wave packet of a free particle.
authors: Felipe S. Esc\'orcio, Hermano Velten

papers.title: Programmable Preparation of Topological Entangled States
papers.abstract: Programmable preparation of entangled quantum states is a central requirement for scalable quantum information processing, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing. Topological photonic platforms offer an attractive route towards robust quantum-state generation by encoding information in symmetry- protected optical modes, yet the generated entangled states are typically dictated by the lattice geometry and therefore lack programmability. Here we demonstrate programmable preparation of topological entangled states by inverse engineering the nonlinear optical pump profile of an integrated photonic lattice. Our approach enables deterministic control over both the dimensionality and modal structure of the generated entangled state while preserving its topological character. We experimentally realize silicon photonic topological superlattices in which the nonlinear generation pathway itself becomes programmable via tailored excitations. The superlattices host a multiband manifold of co localized topological interface modes, while coherently controlled inputs synthesize pump superpositions within this protected basis. We showcase this principle by selectively addressing topological biphoton eigenstates, steering correlations to produce a desired target state in a high-dimensional Hilbert space, and inverse-designing pump states that generate targeted Schmidt dimensionalities. Site-resolved two-photon correlation measurements remain reproducible across nominally identical fabricated devices, demonstrating robustness to realistic nanofabrication-induced disorder. Programmable preparation of topological entangled states establishes a pathway towards exploiting topological photonic modes as application-specific quantum resources, enabling tailored input states for high-dimensional quantum communication, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing.
authors: M. Javad Zakeri, Alaric Pan, Darren D Hudson, Andrea Blanco-Redondo

papers.title: The Classical Boundary of Quantum Computation: History-Resolved Causal Stochastic Machines and the Cost of Classicalization
papers.abstract: What separates quantum computation from classical computation when a classical model may retain every branch history and arbitrary causal memory? We study this question using history-resolved causal stochastic machines (HCSMs), which describe positive causal history laws. Probabilistic Turing machines (PTMs) embed in stochastic-ensemble models (SEnMs), which in turn embed in HCSMs. We prove that HCSM history laws coincide exactly with the fixed-basis, prefix-preserving diagonal sector of ideal quantum processes, denoted by $\mathsf{PTM}_{\rm proc}$ and distinguished here from algorithmic quantum Turing machines (QTMs). Coherent quantum processes extend strictly beyond this sector. The boundary is already visible in reversibility. Born-probability shadows of unitary gates preserve inverse composition exactly for basis permutations with phases. Outside this class, an exact positive stochastic simulation that supports universal quantum continuations must retain predictive information absent from visible probabilities. An inverse-recovery identity quantifies this phase ledger, and universal continuation forces the retained probability law to be tomographically sufficient for the quantum state. Under continuous full-state encoding assumptions, this requirement yields quantum-state dimension lower bounds. The familiar slogan $\mathsf{PTM}\subseteq\mathsf{QTM}$ is thereby sharpened into a precise classical boundary and a no-free-classicalization principle. Complete classical branching does not remove the predictive information needed to represent quantum coherence.
authors: Kyoungho Cho, Junghee Ryu, Minsu Kim, Jeongho Bang

papers.title: Quantumness of Entanglement in Schwarzschild de Sitter Spacetime
papers.abstract: We investigate genuine multipartite entanglement and genuine tripartite nonlocality of a noisy generalized GHZ state in Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime. The genuine multipartite concurrence and optimized Svetlichny parameter are employed to characterize these two quantum correlations. It is shown that the black hole and cosmological event horizons redistribute genuine multipartite entanglement differently among the physically accessible and inaccessible reduced states, while Svetlichny violation occurs only in the physically accessible state. We find that genuine multipartite entanglement can survive in the physically inaccessible states even when genuine tripartite nonlocality is absent. In addition, initial white noise suppresses both correlations, with Svetlichny nonlocality surviving over a narrower parameter region. Furthermore, in the Nariai limit, under the normalization adopted here, the correlations become concentrated in the physically accessible state. These results demonstrate the different robustness of genuine multipartite entanglement and genuine tripartite nonlocality under horizon effects and initial noise.
authors: Sumeng Wang, Xiaofen Huang

papers.title: Asymptotic evaluation of multidimensional oscillatory integrals
papers.abstract: Oscillatory integrals appear throughout physics, from diffraction and gravitational lensing to real-time path integrals. Their asymptotic evaluation is complicated by the need to determine which real and complex saddle points contribute, and how they are connected by Stokes phenomena. In multiple dimensions, this traditionally requires computing steepest descent manifolds in a high-dimensional complex space. Here, we develop an algebraic alternative for integrals with polynomial and rational exponents. Using integration by parts and Brieskorn reduction, we construct a finite-dimensional Gauss-Manin system that generates the asymptotic expansion of all saddle points. Its Borel transform yields a Fuchsian system, whose mondromy determines the Stokes constants and hence the adjacency of the saddle points. Combined with the recent South-East rule, this identifies the contributing saddles and enables superasymptotic and hyperasymptotic approximations without computing gradient flows. We demonstate the method for the parabolic umbilic diffraction integral and a Lorentzian lens as examples, obtaining agreement to machine precision. The methods are implemented in an accompanying open-source Julia package Resurgence.jl
authors: Samuel Crew, Job Feldbrugge

papers.title: Development of a fabrication-to-benchtop process for SiN-based quantum devices
papers.abstract: Silicon nitride has emerged as a key material for the advancement of future quantum communication and computational devices. However, challenges persist in establishing a comprehensive development process, spanning from fabrication to optical characterization, essential for advancing these devices to their next stage of potential. Maintaining control over the entire process, from start to finish, alongside device modeling, enables more efficient and timely iteration and optimization. Here we introduce a fabrication-to-benchtop process. We employ an in-house stoichiometric recipe for device fabrication and conduct comprehensive characterization of optical losses and material properties. Understanding and controlling the refractive index of the device are vital for predicting device geometries and group indices. Implementing the refractive indices of our fabricated devices, we simulate microring resonators and demonstrate their application in generating optical solitons.
authors: Connor Kupchak, Abubaker Tareki, Tara Moradi, Patrick Laferriere, Niall Tait, Khaled Mnaymneh

papers.title: Hidden Supersymmetry in AdS/QCD models for Fermions
papers.abstract: We show that the chiral modes splitted from the Dirac equation satisfying Schrodinger-like equations in the context of deformed AdS/QCD model are isospectral, since the chiral effective potentials are SUSY partners. In particular, we show how to perform truncations of these potentials that preserve isospectrality of the chiral modes. Following this prescription, we compare a quadratic approximation of the deformed AdS model with the dressed soft wall model for fermions and show how the spectra of both models can coincide.
authors: Rafael A. Costa-Silva, Henrique Boschi-Filho

papers.title: Poisson-Dirichlet statistics for the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
papers.abstract: For $T > 0$ large, let $\tau$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$ and let $\sigma = \sigma(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. For the Riemann zeta function $\zeta$, we study the Gibbs measure with density proportional to $|\zeta(\sigma + \mathrm{i}\tau + \mathrm{i} h)|^{\beta}$ on $I_{\theta} := [ - (\log{T})^{\theta},(\log{T})^{\theta}]$, for every $\theta > 0$ and $\beta > 0$. As $\beta$ increases, the Gibbs measure increasingly favors positions where $|\zeta|$ is large, providing a way to study the spatial organization of extreme values. Under explicit conditions on the rate at which $\sigma$ approaches the critical line, a phase transition is established at the critical inverse temperature $\beta_{c}(\theta) := 2\sqrt{1 + \theta}$. The limiting distribution of the correlation (or overlap) between the field values at two positions sampled from the Gibbs measure is concentrated at $0$ when $\beta \leq \beta_{c}(\theta)$, and assigns masses $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ and $1 - \beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ to $0$ and $1$, respectively, when $\beta > \beta_{c}(\theta)$. Joint convergence of the overlaps is also established, with the limiting arrays described by Poisson-Dirichlet weights in the low-temperature regime. The Ghirlanda-Guerra identities, which provide recursive relations for the joint overlap distributions, are established in the limit, uniformly for bounded deterministic observables of the sampled positions. All our results are established independently of the Riemann hypothesis.
authors: Fr\'ed\'eric Ouimet

papers.title: On the relationship between the POVM framework and the no-signaling hypothesis
papers.abstract: The quantum foundations literature contains dozens of "no-signaling" arguments that rely on the Born rule or, more generally, the positive operator-valued measure (POVM) framework to show that the resources of non-relativistic quantum mechanics (NRQM) cannot be used to send superluminal signals. What these arguments typically establish, however, is not a prohibition on superluminal signaling per se, but the seemingly stronger claim that signaling at any speed between mutually isolated systems is forbidden. This paper gives a precise formulation of this claim, the no-signaling hypothesis, and investigates the following converse question: under what additional assumptions does it imply that all experimental outcome probabilities are described by POVMs? Surprisingly few are needed: given the standard NRQM representation of composite experiments and two textbook claims about marginal probabilities, the no-signaling hypothesis is equivalent to the universality of the POVM framework. More broadly, by formalizing the relevant concepts and deriving the logical relationships between them, the paper shows that the no-signaling hypothesis can be used to derive most, though not all, of the probability-generating fragment of NRQM. The resulting map of implications clarifies which common postulates of NRQM are logically interrelated and which can be modified independently.
authors: Will Cavendish

papers.title: Pressure-Dependent hcp-to-fcc Phase Transition Path Derived from Exact Lattice Summations over Inverse Power Law Potentials
papers.abstract: We investigate the phase transition between hexagonal close-packed (hcp) and face-centered cubic (fcc) structures along the Burgers-Bain transformation path at pressures up to several hundred gigapascals. We consider a hierarchy of interatomic potentials, from $(n,m)$-Lennard-Jones potentials to extended Lennard-Jones two-body interactions in terms of inverse-power expansions and the Axilrod-Teller-Muto three-body term, alongside density functional theory (DFT) calculations for solid argon. For inverse-power potentials, free energies are evaluated through exact lattice sums and efficient integral representations based on generalizations of the Epstein zeta function to anisotropic interaction kernels, followed by lattice-parameter optimization. This methodology enables an accurate determination of the pressure-dependent Burgers-Bain minimum-energy path and the associated activation barrier for the phase transition. The transformation exhibits pronounced symmetry breaking connecting the Burgers and Bain paths, a feature confirmed by DFT calculations. At high pressure, the hcp-to-fcc activation barrier increases approximately linearly with pressure, owing to the dominant pressure-volume contribution. Including entropy and anharmonic effects yields excellent agreement with experimental temperature-dependent volumes up to the melting point. DFT results also highlight the increasing importance of many-body interactions under compression. Whereas two-body potentials predict that the path passes through the body-centered cubic (bcc) structure only at very high pressures, DFT generally predicts a pathway that bypasses bcc. The Axilrod-Teller-Muto term slightly reduces this discrepancy. Furthermore, DFT performs better at high pressures, where dispersion forces become less important.
authors: Tage W. Maltby, Andres Robles-Navarro, Jonathan K. Hartlaub, Andreas A. Buchheit, {\O}ivind Wilhelmsen, Morten Hammer, Peter Schwerdtfeger

papers.title: Chirality-resolved imaging of spin waves with a quantum spin
papers.abstract: Spin waves carry their propagation direction in the handedness of their circularly polarized stray field, a property inaccessible to scalar magnetometers. In the Damon-Eshbach surface wave of an in-plane magnetized film, the dipolar field above the film rotates with a handedness fixed by the direction of travel. The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre in diamond is an intrinsic polarization analyser: a right-handed field about the NV axis drives one spin transition, and a left-handed field drives the other, in both the ground and the excited state. Here, we exploit the two excited-state transitions, which lie inside the spin-wave band of yttrium iron garnet (YIG), as a pair of chirality channels and image Damon-Eshbach waves in both directions. Because reflection from an etched boundary reverses the handedness, the incident and reflected waves appear as two lines in one spectrum and are imaged separately. In the ground state, the same rule applies, and the selected field drives Rabi oscillations, a route to chirality-selective control of the NV spin by magnons. Reading the two channels gives the direction of a spin wave at one point, without a phase reference. This advances chirality-resolved quantum sensing and provides insight into chiral spin-wave dynamics.
authors: Enbo Zhang, Tiancheng Zheng, Bo-Yuan Yang, Shreyes Nallan, Chengchao Xu, Mark Ku, Jian-Gang Zhu

papers.title: Quantum approximate stochastic combinatorial optimisation
papers.abstract: Two-stage stochastic combinatorial optimisation concerns discrete decisions made before all relevant information is known. An initial decision is made; once uncertainty is resolved, it can be adapted to the realised scenario, at a cost. The aim is to find the initial decision that minimises the upfront cost plus the expected cost of optimal adaptation. The first-stage decision problem is often NP-hard, and computing the expected minimum recourse cost can be $\#\mathrm{P}$-hard for a single first-stage candidate. We introduce Quantum Approximate Stochastic Combinatorial Optimisation (QASCO), a variational quantum-walk ansatz that coherently incorporates scenario-dependent recourse into its dynamics to search over first-stage decisions without explicitly evaluating expected minimum recourse costs. We demonstrate QASCO for MaxCut with stochastic edge weights, obtain a circuit with polynomial per-layer gate complexity, and study the ansatz via exact state-vector simulation. Across the instances considered, QASCO concentrates amplitude more effectively on stochastic-optimal first-stage decisions than a previously proposed two-stage QAOA construction. We further show that the ansatz can be calibrated using a depth-independent number of parameters and applied to unseen instances without further circuit-parameter optimisation, including joint decision--scenario--recourse spaces spanning more than $2^{32}$ configurations. Under a query-cost model, comparison with the tested classical heuristics using sample-average approximations of the expected minimum recourse cost shows that QASCO more reliably reaches globally optimal first-stage solutions while requiring fewer cut evaluations. These results show how to incorporate scenario-dependent recourse into the ansatz dynamics, providing a general framework for variational quantum walks in two-stage stochastic combinatorial optimisation.
authors: Edric Matwiejew, Paulo E. Santos, Jingbo B. Wang, Ugo Varetto

papers.title: Asymmetric multiscalar fixed points from equiangular tight frames
papers.abstract: In their work on multiscalar RG flows, Rychkov and Stergiou posed the question of whether there exist real fixed points of the one-loop renormalization group for scalar field theories in $d=4-\epsilon$ which respect no extra symmetry beyond the universal $\mathbb{Z}_2$ field inversion. In this note, we report on a construction of a large number of such fixed points in the theory of $22001$ scalar fields, thus resolving the question. The construction uses the geometry of an equiangular tight frame in order to reduce the (up to two-loop) fixed point equation to a two-dimensional space of couplings without assuming any extra symmetry. The main technical hurdle is then to establish the existence of such a frame whose corresponding lines preserve no symmetry. This can be achieved using the Steiner frame construction of Fickus, Mixon, and Tremain.
authors: Christopher Beem

papers.title: Quantum-Assisted Unambiguous Discrimination of Pure States with Robustness Bounds
papers.abstract: We propose a hybrid quantum-classical framework for the unambiguous discrimination of pure states by combining the noisy intermediate-scale quantum semidefinite program solver (NSS) with the reciprocal-state representation. In NSS, a given semidefinite program (SDP) is represented within a subspace spanned by chosen ansatz states, with the required quantities estimated using quantum circuits, and the resulting optimization is performed classically. This makes NSS naturally applicable to discrimination problems involving circuit-prepared states, as finding a discrimination measurement can be formulated as an SDP. By choosing the discriminated states themselves as the ansatz and exploiting the reciprocal-state representation, the general matrix-variable NSS formulation is reduced to an optimization over N scalar variables, where N is the number of discriminated states. The resulting formulation reduces the number of optimization variables and positive-semidefinite constraints compared with the original NSS formulation. We further establish robustness guarantees against Gram matrix estimation errors, including a rescaling procedure that guarantees a valid positive operator-valued measure (POVM) under bounded perturbations. The resulting bounds quantify both the deviation in average success probability and violations of the no-error condition using only the estimated Gram matrix, its SDP solution, and a characterized perturbation bound, without access to the ideal Gram matrix. Numerical simulations validate the derived robustness bounds and characterize finite-shot scaling. We also perform experiments on IBM quantum hardware to estimate pairwise overlaps, and then evaluate the performance of the resulting POVMs.
authors: Jinhyeok Heo, Dongkeun Lee, Junghee Ryu, Minjin Choi

papers.title: Streamwise dispersion with interphase mass transfer through a tube
papers.abstract: Reactive solute transport in shear flows is of broad importance in chemical engineering, liquid--solid chromatography, and environmental mechanics, particularly in flow reactors and fluidic devices involving interphase mass transfer. Based on the recently developed streamwise dispersion theory for inert solutions (Guan & Chen, 2024, J. Fluid Mech., vol. 980, A33), we present an analytical model for reactive dispersion of chemically active solutes characterized by first-order, irreversible surface reactions. The extension is not a simple perturbation because the reactive boundary destroys mass conservation with streamwise and radial derivatives coupled. The model establishes how the microscopic kinetic reactivity and radial eigenmodes combine to determine a newly defined (effective) local exchange rate. We derive rigorous explicit solutions for the local moments, concentration, and phenomenological transport coefficients at arbitrary reactivity, in quantitative agreement with numerical simulations across all regimes. For tube Poiseuille flows, we reveal pre-asymptotic behaviours including sign-changing radial exchange, reactivity-enhanced drift, reactivity-reduced dispersivity, and non-Gaussian concentration profiles. Small- and large-Damk\"ohler-number asymptotics for the local and global transport coefficients identify the reaction-limited and diffusion-limited regimes, connecting the conservative case to the Dirichlet limit at infinite reactivity. This streamwise perspective could advance our understanding of macroscale transport in chemically active systems.
authors: Mingyang Guan, Zhan Wang

papers.title: Encodings and Node Architecture: Lessons from the Fault-Tolerant Distributed Transversal Fanout
papers.abstract: An encoding choice specifies the quantum error-correcting code used to encode logical qubits at a given node. Different encoding choices may differ in the number of physical qubits, the number of encoded logical qubits, the code distance, and the available fault-tolerant operations. We study different encodings for a distributed transversal fanout operation and look at its implications on node architecture. Our experiments suggest that an encoding with higher distance, even if requiring more ebits, can yield a lower logical error rate for distributed operations, and that ``upgrading'' an encoding prior to distributed operations and having a cache, as part of node architecture, for qubits can be useful for distributed operations.
authors: Seng W. Loke

papers.title: Parity-dependent sublattice structure of local $2\times2$ correlations in domino tilings of the Aztec diamond
papers.abstract: We study local $2\times2$ correlations in uniformly random domino tilings of the Aztec diamond $\mathrm{AZ}(n)$, a dimer model with frozen corners and a liquid region bounded by the Arctic circle, and compare them with the square chessboard. For every elementary square the probabilities $P_H$ and $P_V$ of the two coverings by a pair of parallel dominoes satisfy $P_H=P_V=P_1P_2+P_3P_4$, where $P_1,\dots,P_4$ are the probabilities of the four surrounding edges. This known identity, a case of Kuo's graphical condensation, reduces the spatial profile of $P_H$ to single-edge probabilities, which we compute exactly from the inverse Kasteleyn matrix for all squares of $\mathrm{AZ}(n)$. The squares form two interleaved sublattices, distinguished by the color of their lower-left cell. The parity of $n$ decides which sublattice dominates near the center: the one containing the central square for odd $n$, and the other one for even $n$. This sign rule holds for the averaged sublattice contrast for all $4\le n\le22$. It also fixes the location of the global maximum of $P_H$, which lies at or next to the center for odd $n$ and several lattice spacings away for even $n$. Within the central sublattice, the preferred square follows a mod-4 pattern that matches the exactly pinned mean height of the center. On the $L\times L$ chessboard the same rule holds with $n$ replaced by the half-width $L/2$, but the contrast is two to six times weaker, the central edge probability never equals $1/4$, and the maxima of $P_H$ are pinned to the corners. The exact $1/4$ values and the interior, parity-selected maxima are therefore features of the Aztec geometry.
authors: Chaeyeon Kim, Suhwan Yoo, Jeehoon Choi, Hee Young Kwon, Changyeon Won

papers.title: Quantum Tsallis Entropy Estimation: Near-Optimal Bounds and High-Precision Improvements
papers.abstract: Estimating statistical properties of probability distributions is a fundamental problem in statistics and theoretical computer science. We develop quantum algorithms for estimating the $q$-Tsallis entropy $\mathrm{H}_q^{\mathrm{Tsa}}(P) =\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n p_i^q-1}{1-q}$ when $0<q<1$, given purified quantum query access to a distribution $P$ on $[n]$. When $0<q\leq \frac{1}{2}$, we provide a quantum algorithm with query complexity $\widetilde{O}\rbra{\left(\frac{n}{\varepsilon}\right)^{\frac{1}{2q}}}$, which is optimal up to polylogarithmic factors. When $\frac{1}{2}<q<1$, we introduce a two-stage simultaneous probability estimation procedure, yielding a quantum algorithm with query complexity $\widetilde{O}\left(\frac{n^{\frac12+\frac{1}{2q}}}{\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{2q}}}+\frac{n^{1-q}}{\varepsilon}\right)$, which improves the result given by Chen et al. (ICALP 2026) when $\varepsilon=O\rbra{n^{1-2q}}$.
authors: Chengshen Gao, Zongxing Xiong, Lvzhou Li

papers.title: Leading-twist proton parton distribution amplitude from scalar and axial-vector diquark correlations
papers.abstract: We compute the leading-twist proton parton distribution amplitude (PDA) using algebraic representations of the nucleon Faddeev wave function inspired by perturbation-theory integral representations. The PDA is obtained from a light-front projection of the covariant quark--diquark Faddeev amplitude and analysed in terms of its scalar- and axial-vector-diquark components. We derive analytic expressions for the corresponding diquark distribution amplitudes and their contributions to the proton PDA. The resulting distribution is broad and concave, with its maximum $(x_1,x_2,x_3)\approx(0.55,0.20,0.25)$ displaced from the symmetric configuration $(1/3,1/3,1/3)$, which corresponds to the maximum of the perturbative-QCD asymptotic form. Scalar-diquark correlations generate a strong asymmetry in the longitudinal momentum distribution, whereas axial-vector correlations redistribute momentum among the valence quarks and significantly reduce this asymmetry. We calculate low-order Mellin moments and obtain a compact parametrisation of the proton PDA at the hadronic scale, $\mu_0=0.51\,\mathrm{GeV}$. We then perform the leading-order QCD evolution of its normalized shape to $\mu=2\,\mathrm{GeV}$, finding that evolution reduces the momentum asymmetry while preserving a clear imprint of the non-perturbative quark--diquark correlations. The results provide insight into the role of such correlations in shaping the proton light-front structure and furnish non-perturbative input for studies of hard exclusive baryonic processes.
authors: B. Almeida-Zamora, L. Albino, C. Mezrag, J. Segovia

papers.title: Diffusion-controlled reactions with time-dependent surface reactivity
papers.abstract: We investigate diffusion-controlled reactions on a reactive surface with time-dependent reactivity. Starting from a conventional formulation via diffusion equation with Robin boundary condition for the macroscopic concentration of particles, we aim at quantifying how temporal variations of reactivity affect the survival probability and the associated first-reaction time (FRT) of a single particle on the reactive surface. Using an adiabatic description, we first identify five long-time regimes of the first-reaction time distribution, ranging from exponential and stretched-exponential to power-law decay. In particular, sufficiently rapid decay of the reactivity leads to a nonzero probability of never reacting, despite diffusion in a bounded domain. Second, we provide a probabilistic reformulation of this problem and compare it with a different scenario of encounter-dependent reactivity. Our theoretical predictions are validated via extensive Monte Carlo simulations.
authors: Denis S. Grebenkov, Yilin Ye

papers.title: Discrete time crystals and classical logic gates in coupled open Dicke models
papers.abstract: We investigate the dynamics of coupled discrete time crystals (DTCs) in the coupled Dicke model or Dicke dimer (DD) with dissipation. By numerically simulating the mean-field dynamics of the system, we show that coupling two DTCs decreases their oscillation amplitude following a transient relaxation period. For sufficiently strong coupling, the coupled DTCs become unstable, resulting in the system relaxing towards the normal phase (NP). We demonstrate that the relaxation time diverges near the critical coupling strength, suggesting a continuous phase transition. Using the truncated Wigner approximation (TWA), we explore how the dynamics are affected by the introduction of quantum fluctuations. We also consider a scenario in which an NP is briefly coupled to a DTC, seeding the NP to transform into a DTC that is either synchronized or anti-synchronized relative to the DTC. We investigate the robustness of this phenomenon in the presence of noise. Using these results, we propose a scheme to perform NAND and NOR operations with three DTCs by sequentially coupling the input and output sites. We identify the parameter regimes in which the logic gate architecture remains valid, and investigate how the protocol is affected by the presence of quantum fluctuations.
authors: Emmanuel D. G. U, Roy D. Jara Jr., Jayson G. Cosme

papers.title: Concrete Functions in Private Simultaneous Quantum Messages: Quantum Advantages and Structural Limitations
papers.abstract: Private simultaneous quantum messages (PSQM) provide a minimal model of noninteractive secure multiparty quantum computation, yet their communication complexity for concrete functions remains poorly understood. We show that familiar total functions already exhibit both genuine quantum advantages and strong structural limitations. For three-party equality on $n$-bit inputs, which determines whether the players' $n$-bit strings are identical, we construct an entanglement-assisted protocol with asymptotic communication $(1.633\ldots)n$ qubits, whereas every perfectly correct protocol without prior entanglement requires at least $3n$ qubits. For three-bit majority, one shared GHZ state and one transmitted qubit per player suffice for perfect correctness and perfect privacy, reducing the communication from the optimal classical cost of six bits to three qubits. Three-bit AND behaves differently. No perfectly correct and perfectly private protocol exists when the players share an arbitrary three-qubit state, apply arbitrary local unitary encodings, and transmit one qubit each. However, increasing the local dimension overcomes this obstruction: one shared three-qutrit GHZ state and one transmitted qutrit per player yield a one-shot protocol with total communication $3\log_2 3$. Together with the six-bit classical lower bound, this gives a strict quantum communication advantage. More generally, for every $k\geq 3$, we construct a perfectly correct and perfectly private one-shot protocol for $k$-bit AND using one qudit of dimension at most $k$ per player, and hence at most $k\log_2 k$ qubits in total.
authors: Harumichi Nishimura

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions in the Extended Agassi Model
papers.abstract: We investigate dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) in the extended Agassi model following sudden quenches of same level pairing ($\Sigma$), monopole-monopole ($\chi$) and cross level pairing ($\Lambda$) strengths. Using exact diagonalization, we characterize the non-equilibrium dynamics through the Loschmidt echo and intensive return-rate function. Quenches across equilibrium phase boundaries produce cusp-like structures in the return rate that shows non-analyticities with increasing system size. Equilibrium finite size to large scaling identifies the $\chi$-driven transition as a second order phase transition similar to mean-field, Dicke, and Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick (LMG) models critical behaviour with the exponent of the order parameter $\beta \simeq 1/2$, while the $\Sigma$- and $\Lambda$-driven transitions are first order. We further characterize the associated dynamical singularities through a local scaling exponent $\alpha$, with $\alpha_\chi \simeq 2/3$, $\alpha_\Lambda \simeq 1/3$, and $\alpha_\Sigma \simeq 3/2$ of all three parameters. The distinct scaling behaviours across the parameter channels show that dynamical criticality is not determined solely by the equilibrium order of the transition, revealing multiple dynamical scaling regimes. These non-analyticities are associated with the Fisher zeros of the Loschmidt amplitude, which cross the real time axis at critical times and the time derivatives of the return-rate function to characterize the order of DQPTs within the extended Agassi model.
authors: Ritesh Kumar Palai, Rajiv Kumar, Venktesh Singh, Sunil K. Mishra

papers.title: Environment-induced topological reconstruction of black-hole thermodynamics
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic topology describes black-hole (BH) equilibria as zeros, or defects, of a vector field built from the off-shell free energy. Studies with surrounding matter find that the topological class is unchanged, but not how the matter's spatial distribution affects individual equilibria. We ask whether the position of a localized environment can reorganize these equilibria at fixed total topological number. We model the environment as a radially localized energy bump peaked at $a_m$ and add its exterior energy to the generalized off-shell free energy. As $a_m$ varies, defects migrate and are created or annihilated in opposite-charge pairs, a process we call topological reconstruction. It changes the number and stability of equilibrium branches but preserves the total topological number, provided no zero crosses the boundary of the physical domain. We find this in Schwarzschild, Schwarzschild-AdS, Reissner-Nordstr\"om, and Reissner-Nordstr\"om-AdS BHs, with critical positions and required strength that depend on the background. In our examples, the required environmental energy ranges from below $1\%$ of the BH mass to a value comparable to it. The model is an effective fixed-background description without backreaction. Within it, the total topological number cannot capture the environmental response; local defects must be tracked.
authors: Xinyu Zhou, Chen Lan, Zhen-Ming Xu

papers.title: Nonergodicity from Hilbert-Subspace Cloning
papers.abstract: We identify a class of nonintegrable quantum many-body systems composed of single Pauli strings that possess an extensive number of noncommuting local conserved quantities and exhibit partial ergodicity breaking due to exponentially degenerate energy spectra. We show that such systems exhibit a novel mechanism, Hilbert-subspace cloning, where the identical chaotic Hamiltonian acts on each of exponentially many disconnected Hilbert subspaces. Although the dynamics within each clone thermalizes, quantum coherence between clones remains protected and detectable by local observables. Consequently, the long-time behavior of local observables is described by a coherence-preserving partial Gibbs ensemble, where the hidden subsystem retains its initial quantum coherence.
authors: Yuuya Chiba, Ryusuke Hamazaki

papers.title: From quantum emitters to technological platforms: a perspective on semiconductor quantum dots
papers.abstract: Photonic quantum technologies are based on controlled photon states. To generate these, quantum dots have emerged as excellent sources of single and entangled photons. In this Perspective, we briefly review the chronological development of quantum dots as photon sources, from their beginnings as quantum emitters in the early 2000s to the advanced photonic devices being developed today. We highlight the interplay between fundamental research and industrial aspects before discussing the photonic quantum technologies we expect to emerge in the near future.
authors: Klaus D. J\"ons, Dorian A. Gangloff, Doris E. Reiter

papers.title: Multiscale Quantum-Classical Simulation of Protein Autoproteolysis in a Million-Atom Membrane Environment
papers.abstract: Predicting chemical reactions in biomolecules is challenging because reactive centers are embedded within complex environments that strongly influence their energetics and mechanisms. Here, we present a hybrid quantum-classical workflow that combines molecular dynamics, density functional theory, and correlated wavefunction methods, tightly integrating CPUs, GPUs, and quantum processing units (QPUs) to enable simulations across multiple length and accuracy scales. We apply this approach to ADGRG1 autoproteolysis, a maturation reaction in an adhesion G protein-coupled receptor that has not previously been studied using correlated electronic-structure methods. Our simulations treat a biologically realistic system containing more than one million atoms, including the full-length uncleaved receptor embedded in an endoplasmic-reticulum membrane, while incorporating a 54-qubit IQM quantum processor and up to 1,200 NVIDIA H100 GPUs. These results demonstrate how quantum computers can serve as accelerators within scalable scientific workflows, extending correlated electronic-structure methods to biologically relevant systems.
authors: Alexander Orlov, Alexis Ralli, Tim Weaving, Michael Williams de la Bastida, Reuben Martin, Zohim Chandani, Minh Chung, P. V. Sriluckshmy, Fedor Simkovic IV, Luigi Iapichino, Peter J. Love, Christian B. Mendl, Andrea Townsend-Nicholson, Peter V. Coveney

papers.title: Liouvillian Non-Invertible Symmetry
papers.abstract: Non-invertible symmetries extend conventional symmetries beyond group-like transformations and play an important role in quantum field theory and many-body physics.
