In the early stages of learning, we find that a Gaussian description of overlap statistics reduces the learning dynamics to a few collective variables that track learning of the target function's linear and quadratic components. We then estimate the timescale of specialization, when Gaussian closure breaks down and individual learned features begin to strongly correlate with specific target features. We find that specialization in extensive-rank networks is accelerated via a quadratic shielding mechanism, whereby learning the linear and quadratic components of the target function filters gradient fluctuations. We finally describe how the activation function determines the pattern of specialization and characterize the subsequent refinement of learned features. Together, these results show how collective learning gives way to individual feature discovery and clarify when learning in large neural networks admits a simple statistical description.
authors: Shu Zhou, Jean Barbier, Sebastian Goldt

papers.title: Transport and thermalization under noncommuting localized constraints
papers.abstract: We investigate the effects of spatially localized conserved quantities on transport and thermalization in quantum and classical many-body systems. We consider several related models: the integrable quantum Volterra model, its nonintegrable classical limit, and two cellular automata derived from the latter. Although localized constraints are often associated with lattice gauge theories, our models do not admit such an interpretation. In systems with discrete degrees of freedom, these constraints induce uniform fragmentation of the Hilbert or configuration space. In the quantum Volterra model, we derive an exact mapping of the dynamics within each Hilbert-space fragment onto a quantum chiral Potts chain. We find that energy transport is ballistic, with identical transport coefficients across all fragments. In the nonintegrable classical limit, energy transport is diffusive, and we similarly find the diffusion constant to be independent of whether or not the constraints are fixed (resolved). Finally, in the cellular automata, we show that, despite leaving transport unaffected, localized constraints lead to a strong breakdown of local ergodicity.
authors: Amir Nesturov, Attila Tak\'acs, Lenart Zadnik

papers.title: Sampling the XY model with an attention-based neural network
papers.abstract: We present a transformer-based variational autoregressive network for sampling lattice systems with continuous degrees of freedom and apply it to the two-dimensional XY model near the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition. The architecture is combined with physics-informed ingredients: locality-informed attention and approximate probabilities. The resulting sampler significantly outperforms existing neural samplers. We train the model on lattices up to $96\times96$, verify with a mode-dropping estimator that no parts of the configuration space are missed, and reproduce the energy, magnetization and helicity modulus obtained with the traditional Markov Chain Monte Carlo algorithm.
authors: Piotr Bia{\l}as, Christian D. Morales, Tomasz Stebel, Dawid Zapolski

papers.title: Anti-synchronized collective rotation in magnetic colloidal particles under rotating magnetic fields
papers.abstract: Collective synchronization is a common response of interacting magnetic particles subjected to rotating external fields. Here we demonstrate a distinct nonequilibrium state in a two-dimensional cluster of magnetic colloidal particles in which the ordered crystalline core rotates, on average, opposite to the direction of the applied rotating magnetic field, while the defect-rich outer region continues to rotate with the drive. We term this state anti-synchronized collective rotation. By combining structural, spectral, bond-resolved, and layer-resolved torque analyses, we show that anti-synchronization is associated with a broader defect-rich interface, enhanced and dynamically heterogeneous bond deformation, and a reorganization of torque transmission between the surface and the crystalline interior. In the synchronized state, steric torques compensate the opposing dipolar contribution in the outer core, maintaining a positive net interaction torque. In the anti-synchronized state this compensation becomes insufficient, producing a negative net torque in theouter core and enabling core-surface rotational decoupling. Increasing the driving frequency restores coherent rotation through a transition characterized by competing positive- and negative-angular-velocity populations and hysteresis, consistent with a discontinuous, first-order-like dynamical transition. These results demonstrate how deformation and spatial redistribution of interaction torques can generate counter-rotating collective states in driven colloidal matter.
authors: Adithya Bharath, A. V. Anil Kumar

papers.title: Experimental Demonstration of a Balanced Travelling Wave Parametric Amplifier
papers.abstract: Superconducting travelling-wave parametric amplifiers (TWPAs) provide broadband gain, low added noise, and high dynamic range, making them attractive for applications requiring wide instantaneous bandwidth. This is crucial for amplifying multiplexed narrow band signals spread over a wide frequency range, such as qubit resonator arrays, or amplifying inherently wide band signals, such as in spectrometers or radiometers. In many cases, however, the useful bandwidth of a TWPA is limited by the production of the idler tone at an image frequency. For three-wave-mixing (3WM) TWPAs, for example, an input signal at $f_s$ is indistinguishable from one at $f_p - f_s$, which can produce spectral ambiguity when the input spectrum is broadband or not known in advance. We experimentally demonstrate a balanced architecture that doubles the instantaneous image-rejected bandwidth available to a 3WM TWPA by spatially separating the amplified signal from the output pump and generated idler, which resolves the sideband degeneracy. The architecture consists of two amplifiers connected between a pair of 180$^{\circ}$ hybrid couplers, with the signal and pump injected and output through the sum and difference ports, respectively. Using two kinetic-inductance TWPAs, we demonstrate approximately 20 dB of signal gain across nearly an octave of bandwidth, together with pump rejection below --20 dB and an average image rejection of approximately --15 dB over the operating band. These results establish balanced TWPAs as a practical approach to broadband parametric amplification, enabling improved contamination free bandwidth and eliminating the need for complex filtering.
authors: Nikita Klimovich, Peter K. Day, Henry G. Leduc, Boon-Kok Tan

papers.title: Anyonic Neural Network Wavefunctions
papers.abstract: The macroscopic behavior of a non-interacting gas of Abelian anyons has remained unsettled for many decades. Prior numerical methods employing exact diagonalization in the continuum and on the plane have been limited to small system sizes, at most $N = 4$ anyons. Using the rapidly developing technology of neural network wavefunctions, we develop variational ansatze appropriate for studying continuum models of the Abelian anyon gas. The neural network architecture, which we call "AnyNet", is capable of exactly enforcing the non-analytic short-distance behavior induced by the anyonic statistics. We demonstrate excellent agreement with exact diagonalization for $N=4$ anyons, obtain accurate results up to $N = 16$ for intermediate statistics, and study up to $N=20$ for almost-fermionic anyons, matching perturbative results within a 0.4% discrepancy. We use this methodology to study anyons in a harmonic trap, and anyonic atoms as a model for anyon binding to impurities. We study the structure of anyonic wavefunctions as the statistics parameter is varied. We focus on the single-particle density, the pair density, the angular momentum, and the scaling of the wavefunction as multiple anyons coalesce. This work opens doors to understanding the macroscopic behavior of anyons, for which rich phases have been predicted theoretically.
authors: Andres Perez Fadon, Pok Man Tam, Leyna Shackleton

papers.title: Memory effects in the homogenization of a viscous fluid containing elastic particles
papers.abstract: This work deals with a fluid-structure interaction problem involving an incompressible viscous fluid and a periodic array of tiny elastic inclusions in a three-dimensional domain. We focus on a critical regime where the volume fraction of the inclusions tends to zero, but their density and stiffness are scaled so that they still influence the macroscopic behavior. The asymptotic regime depends on the parameter $\gamma=\lim_{\varepsilon\to 0}r_\varepsilon/\varepsilon^3\in [0,+\infty]$, where $\varepsilon$ is the period and $r_\varepsilon$ the inclusion size. For $\gamma=0$ the solid and fluid equations uncouple in the limit. For $\gamma\in (0,+\infty]$, we show that the macroscopic fluid velocity satisfies a Stokes system with memory: the standard Stokes equations are augmented by convolution-in-time terms arising from the elastic vibrations of the inclusions. The existence of the convolution kernels is established for both $\gamma\in(0,+\infty)$ and $\gamma=\infty$ using semigroup theory. For $\gamma=\infty$ the microscopic problem reduces to a purely conservative elastodynamic equation and the kernels can be computed explicitly via spectral decomposition. They are oscillatory and almost-periodic in time, yielding a persistent, non-decaying memory. For $\gamma\in(0,+\infty)$ the microscopic elastodynamic equation is coupled to a local Stokes problem, whose viscous dissipation yields memory kernels that decay to zero at infinity.
authors: J. Casado-D\'{\i}az, A. R. Hormigo-Molina

papers.title: A Universal Lower Bound for the Complexity of Gaussian-Divisible Spin Glasses
papers.abstract: We consider a variant of the spherical mixed spin glass model with non-Gaussian disorder. Specifically, we replace the usual standard Gaussian interaction coefficients with Gaussian-divisible ones, meaning that each coefficient can be expressed as the sum of a standard Gaussian random variable and an independent, non-Gaussian random variable. We show that the annealed complexity of this model is at least the annealed complexity of the standard Gaussian model, if the non-Gaussian part is centered and subexponential.
authors: Pax Kivimae, Benjamin McKenna

papers.title: Quality-of-Transmission Estimation in Quantum Networks: Compute, Simulate, or Learn?
papers.abstract: Future quantum networks will rely on control-plane decisions such as routing, scheduling, entanglement provisioning, purification, and memory allocation. Each decision depends on a timely and reliable estimate of the quality of the entanglement that a candidate path can deliver, with end-to-end fidelity as a central metric. Inspired by the optical-networking experience with quality-of-transmission (QoT) estimation, this article asks when a quantum controller should compute fidelity analytically, simulate it, or learn a surrogate model. The optical analogy is useful but incomplete: optical QoT estimation often predicts a scalar transmission margin, whereas quantum QoT estimation must account for probabilistic entanglement generation, random memory waiting times, decoherence, state consumption, and measurement constraints that can make fidelity a stochastic target. We propose a compute/simulate/learn framework for quantum QoT estimation and illustrate it with a simulation-based proof of concept. Our study shows that analytical composition can be sufficient in simple regimes, that simulation becomes necessary when stochastic memory effects shape the delivered fidelity distribution, and that lightweight learned surrogates can approximate simulator labels at much lower runtime cost for online control. We close with open challenges for deployment, including stochastic targets, sim-to-real transfer, data-generation cost, physics-informed learning, and generalization beyond individual paths to full network topologies.
authors: Anis Bekri, Amar Abane, Van Sy Mai, Abdella Battou, Saddek Bensalem

papers.title: Leveraging verifiable structure in quantum circuits to find more efficient compilations with agentic AI
papers.abstract: We discuss an effective paradigm of utilizing AI agents to better compile quantum circuits when one can constrain bottleneck subroutines to have some form of classically verifiable structure. For example, when critical subroutines are composed exclusively of reversible classical logic, phasing operations, and measurement based uncomputation, one can efficiently simulate execution for classical inputs. This property facilitates efficient certification of approximate circuit synthesis via a form of fuzz testing, provided suitable assumptions on the input distribution. While this pattern was recently exploited to improve quantum cryptanalysis circuits, here we highlight the flexibility of the broader approach by discussing three important applications. (1) The computation of $1/\sqrt{x}$ that bottlenecks real space simulations of the Coulomb operator such as those important for modeling inertial confinement fusion reactors. (2) The decoding of Reed-Solomon codes which bottlenecks the decoded quantum interferometry algorithm when used to approximately solve the optimal polynomial intersection problem. And (3) the quantum look-up tables and controlled application of Givens rotations that bottleneck the most performant quantum algorithms for simulating chemistry in second quantization. We discuss reference implementations of these algorithms and how they can be constrained and verified in the interest of seeding a Kaggle competition designed to accelerate AI-based research into the optimization of their compilation.
authors: Tanuj Khattar, Nicholas C. Rubin, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Guang Hao Low, Ryan Babbush

papers.title: Task-aligned spectral inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits
papers.abstract: Parameterized quantum circuits are widely investigated in quantum machine learning, yet how their architecture can provide task-aligned inductive biases remains poorly understood. We study data reuploading quantum circuits with two distinct inputs: a signal that varies between samples and a fixed, task-defined spectral query that specifies how the signal should be probed. We show that encoding the query can change the circuit's hypothesis class over the signal by modulating how its existing signal frequencies are combined, without introducing new sample-dependent information. This mechanism matches tasks built on nonuniform Fourier transforms, whose evaluation frequencies specify the query and whose sampling positions guide its encoding. We examine this connection in a classification task inspired by synthetic aperture radar, where acquisition geometry determines a query for classifying unfocused spectral patches before image formation. Across small-scale spectral and radar-like tasks, aligned queries improve learning from limited data over parameter-matched circuits with mismatched or absent queries. These results provide a route from known spectral task structure to the design and validation of inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits.
authors: Felix Frohnert, Adri\'an P\'erez-Salinas, Sebastian Lange, Marcus Schwaebisch, Evert van Nieuwenburg, Vedran Dunjko

papers.title: Uniform restriction lower bounds and nongeodesic common nodal curves in integrable systems
papers.abstract: We construct a family of real analytic metrics on the two-torus, for which a fixed embedded nongeodesic circle is a nodal component of infinitely many real Laplace eigenfunctions. The examples address a question asked by Bourgain-Rudnick \cite{BR11}, and give a negative answer to the question asked by Toth-Zelditch \cite{TZ21} and Han \cite{Han}: whether a curve shared by infinitely many nodal sets must be geodesic. To explain the restriction obstruction, we prove uniform $L^2$ lower bounds for joint eigenfunctions of quantum completely integrable (QCI) systems under transverse crossing and isolation of a tangential characteristic branch, then extend to multi-branch setting. The results are used to characterize the possible joint nodal curves in the Liouville tori, narrowing down the choices. Finally, the counterexample realizes one possibility for which cancellation happens exactly on a nongeodesic curve.
authors: Xianchao Wu, Xiao Xiao

papers.title: Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor
papers.abstract: Quantum error correction can suppress logical errors exponentially with code distance when physical noise is below threshold. Realizing this on hardware requires tight coordination among quantum gates, mid-circuit measurements, and qubit coherence. Device variation, noise asymmetry, and correlations across space and time complicate the translation of these capabilities into logical error suppression. Here, we study rotated surface-code memory on an IBM Nighthawk r2 processor. Performance varies across tested processor placements, which we attribute to differences in qubit quality. We optimize the code by combining short readout, fused measurement and reset, and an XX echo on data qubits during ancilla readout. Compared with standard readout without reset or echo, the optimized syndrome extraction circuit reduces the median per-round logical error rate by factors of 3.8 in the X basis and 1.4 in the Z basis. In memory experiments of up to 150 rounds, the distance advantage weakens, alongside long-lived correlations that may reflect a persistent error component. Under our optimization recipe, increasing the protected distance from 3 to 6 while holding the other distance fixed reduces the per-round logical error rate from 0.53% to 0.24% in Z memory and from 0.52% to 0.22% in X memory. The corresponding error-suppression factors under maximum-likelihood decoding are 1.68 and 1.85. These results connect circuit compilation and optimization to surface-code memory performance and limitations, and motivate QPU and QEC circuit codesign for fault-tolerant quantum computing primitives on current cloud hardware.
authors: Shuwen Kan, Aaron Hoyt, Sean Garner, Ethan Vo, Adrian Harkness, Rod Rofougaran, Zefan Du, Chenxu Liu, Norm Tubman, Ying Mao, Samuel Stein

papers.title: Analyticity of the correlation length in subcritical FK-percolation and Potts models
papers.abstract: We prove that the correlation length of FK-percolation and Potts models on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is analytic in the whole subcritical regime of parameters. Our proof makes use of the identification of the polar dual of the mass with the solution of an equation involving the leading eigenvalue of the FK--Ruelle operator, introduced in the context of Ornstein--Zernike theory in Campanino, Ioffe and Velenik (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2003), and crucially relies on Kato's theory of analytic perturbation of linear operators. As a consequence of this result, we prove that the correlation length cannot be invariant by rotation except at countably many values of the temperature parameter in the subcritical phase.
authors: Lucas D'Alimonte, Lo\"ic Gassmann
